result.title: A Rank-One Bypass of Fixed Linear Erasure
result.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Child Safety in AI (poster). 10 pages, 3 figures
result.summary: Linear concept erasure can make a target unreadable to a specified family of linear classifiers applied to a model's current internal features. In an open-weight release, however, an attacker can modify the layers that produce those features. We study a fixed affine erasure layer whose upstream model is allowed to change. If the layer transmits even one direction visible to an allowed downstream classifier, the attacker can write a target score into that direction and carry it through the layer. We show that this condition is also necessary, and that for a nonconstant linear target score the required change is a rank-one affine update. Across six CIFAR-10 class-pair tasks, the route restores nearly all pre-erasure target performance and can leave a deployed benign linear head's scores unchanged to numerical tolerance. We then price the attack: with eight target labels and 2,000 unlabelled calibration examples, a 10% mean relative feature edit yields 79.8% test accuracy, which is 91.2% of the fitted score's gain over chance; tighter edit limits sharply reduce success. Linear guardedness therefore remains a valid guarantee about the current representation, but it is not by itself a tamper-resistance guarantee for an editable open-weight model.

AI.brief_summary: 研究固定仿射概念擦除层在上游模型可被修改时的脆弱性，证明只要该层仍传递一个对下游线性分类器可见的方向，攻击者就能注入目标分数，且所需改动是一个秩一仿射更新；并在 CIFAR-10 上量化恢复效果与编辑成本。
AI.relevance_reason: 对 LVR 中以线性探针或线性擦除判定 latent 是否携带某信息是直接警示：线性不可读并不等于该信息已从内部状态移除；其秩一仿射干预思路也可能供核查表示方向的因果作用，但用于推理状态仍需核查。
